neighboring_unit_entries.title: Repeated integration by parts moves incomplete-beta parameters and exposes an arbitrarily extendable half-plane
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The incomplete beta integral is recursively decomposed into finitely many boundary terms plus a shifted remainder. Applying this to each Fourier mode extends the expression to Re(s)>2-M, so increasing M now genuinely enlarges the continuation domain.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: The classical Euler-Maclaurin proof succeeds because increasing remainder order moves the convergence boundary, whereas the direct q-version is pinned by q^{x(s-1)}. Fourier decomposition and the substitution q^x=u create beta integrals whose integration-by-parts order does move that boundary, after which the q-limit reconstructs the original classical continuation.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The transfer depends on uniform Fourier convergence, mode bounds, and formula-sensitive limit interchange established in this source; it is not a generic license to replace every blocked remainder by a Fourier expansion.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: The proof establishes pointwise classical convergence, yet the near-zero examples show that enormous truncations can remain badly conditioned before eventual convergence. A valid deformation can therefore be conceptually exact while computationally ineffective in sensitive regions.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: In the q-to-1 limit, the Fourier-beta continuation reconstructs the classical Euler-Maclaurin formula term by term: mode sums become Bernoulli corrections, the surviving oscillatory remainder becomes the periodic-Bernoulli integral, and the other beta families vanish at the available scaling.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Using the elementary limits for log q/(1-q), (1-q)^k(s-1+delta n)^k, and (1-q^x)/(1-q), the source takes q to 1 in the continued mode formula for Re(s)>2-M. Fourier identities convert finite mode sums into Bernoulli-number terms and the final mode integral into the periodic-Bernoulli remainder. The beta terms with second parameters -s and -s+1 vanish because they carry lower powers of 1-q. The resulting expression is exactly the classical Euler-Maclaurin formula (11); arbitrary M establishes lim zeta_q(s)=zeta(s) throughout C except s=1.
directed.conceptual_reading: The proof closes by showing compatibility of representations, not merely equality of final values. Boundary terms, Fourier modes, and the remainder all have classical counterparts, so the deformation forgets q while preserving the analytic-continuation decomposition.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge chain is q-asymptotics -> Fourier coefficient identities -> Bernoulli corrections and periodic remainder -> classical Euler-Maclaurin continuation. Equality with formula (11) is the proof certificate.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The conclusion is pointwise and excludes the pole; it supplies no uniform rate or numerical conditioning guarantee. For each chosen M the calculation begins on Re(s)>2-M, and coverage of the plane uses the freedom to take M arbitrarily large.
directed.uncertainty: Exact powers of 1-q, Fourier/Bernoulli normalization, factorials, and the remainder sign are formula-sensitive and extraction-damaged. Proof-level reuse requires PDF verification.
